
### adding associativity 

::: {.r-stack .my-full}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/assocPattern.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="a 2-way set associative cache with 2 byte blocks and 2 sets. The cache has two rows, labeled with indexes 0 and 1, and two columns. Each block (intersection of a row and column) has a valid bit, a tag, and a value field. This structure gives multiple places to put values with the same index, avoiding the need for misses when there are two active values with the same set (a conflict miss)."}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/assocPattern.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Each row of this cache is called a _set_. In this case, we have a set 0 and a set 1."}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/assocPattern.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Each column of this cache is called a _way_. In this case, we have a way 0 and a way 1."}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/assocPattern.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="We can apply the same formulas as before: We have S = 2 = 2^s sets, so s = 1 set index bit. We have B = 2 = 2^b byte block size, so b = 1 (block) offset bit; we have t = m - (s + b) = 6 tag bits."}

:::

### associative lookup possibilities 


* none of the blocks for the index are valid
* none of the valid blocks for the index match the tag 

   * something else is stored there

* one of the blocks for the index is valid and matches the tag
